reason: Source expressly defines N complex doublets with Y=1/2 interacting with ordinary gauge bosons and matter in the standard way; N=3 gives a complete gauge-matter class independent of scalar potential symmetry.

claims.locator: Section2.1, PDF p.3, first two paragraphs and Eq.(1); Introduction PDFpp1-2
claims.fact: N complex Higgs doublets with Y=1/2; N=3 in this paper. They interact with gauge bosons and matter fields in standard way. Expand expressly inherited SM fermion/gauge baseline: three Q,u^c,d^c,L,e^c families and colour-singlet Higgs doublets. Retain SM colour even though paper studies only scalar potential. Discrete Higgs-family choices do not change gauge-matter identity.

limitations: The paper focuses on scalar symmetry classification, not a complete Yukawa/Lagrangian inventory. Standard SM matter is a declared baseline expansion justified by Section2.1, not independently tabulated; global/discrete symmetry distinctions are outside this catalogue.
